Christine Fang, also known as Fang Fang or Christine Fang Fang, is a suspected Chinese intelligence operative (honeytrap) who targeted and cultivated close relationships with emerging U.S. politicians, most notably Rep. Eric Swalwell, between 2011 and 2015. She engaged in fundraising, placed interns, and left the U.S. in 2015 during a federal investigation. Key details regarding the suspected intelligence operative include: Targeting Politicians: Christine Fang targeted Bay Area and Midwestern politicians, including Rep. Eric Swalwell, Rep. Judy Chu, Rep. Mike Honda, and former Fremont Mayor Bill Harrison. Activities: She helped fundraise for Swalwell's 2014 campaign, placed at least one intern in his office, and interacted with him at multiple events for years. Affiliations: She was a student at California State University East Bay, where she was president of the Chinese Student Association and active in campus-based Asian Pacific Islander political groups. Investigation: Federal investigators were tracking her activities; she unexpectedly left the U.S. in mid-2015 amid the probe. Relationship Status: She had sexual relations with at least two Midwestern mayors, according to reports. Case Status: As of 2026, the investigation into her connections has resurfaced in political discourse. Other Individuals Named "Fang Fang"It is important to distinguish this individual from other people named Fang Fang, including: Fang Fang (Writer): A renowned Chinese author (pen name of Wang Fang) known for her Wuhan Diary during the 2020 COVID-19 lockdown. Fang Fang (Geographer): A professor at Northeastern University specializing in urban greenery. Fang Fang (Lawyer): A partner at Baker McKenzie in Palo Alto.
